prompt: A Cortex-M4 device running under an emulated target keeps its settings in a two-page NOR flash with a programming model that only clears bits: an erase fills a 256-byte page with 0xFF, a program can only turn 1s into 0s, and a brownout can stop the device after any erase or program, leaving that operation half applied. The shipped config_store.c erases its only page and rewrites a single record, so a power cut during a save destroys the last good configuration. Implement config_load/config_save against src/config_store.h so that a save is durable: the previous committed record survives a brownout at every erase and program of the new one, a torn record never validates, wear is spread across both pages, and a record written with the legacy schema 1 still loads. src/flash_port.c is the only path to flash and journals every operation; a boot that exhausts the harness power budget dies at that operation, and the harness replays the journal to rebuild the image (a torn operation is applied to half of its bytes) before booting again.

requirements: two page NOR flash model with 256-byte erase granularity, one-way bit programming, and per-page erase counters
power budget consumed by every erase and program, with the device dying exactly at the exhausted operation
journal of erase and program operations replayed by the harness with half-application for the interrupted operation
record contract in src/config_store.h: status 1 committed, 0 nothing committed, -1 torn or corrupt
legacy schema 1 record written by the harness into a blank image and loaded by the candidate's own loader
paired same-model skill/no-skill execution from the identical starting snapshot
